label: prop:p-vs-np-boundary
title: $\mathrm{P} \neq \mathrm{NP}$ as jet horizon opacity
html:
Proposition. \mathrm{P} \neq \mathrm{NP} as jet horizon opacity

Conjecture (\mathrm{P} versus \mathrm{NP} as boundary emptiness). Let L = \hat{\beta} be the closure of a braid \beta encoding a decision problem. Let \mathcal{H}_c(L, q) denote its computational boundary.

  \mathrm{P} = \mathrm{NP} \Longleftrightarrow \mathcal{H}_c(L, q) = \varnothing \text{ for every NP link } L

Consequently, \mathrm{P} \neq \mathrm{NP} if and only if there exists an NP-complete link L carrying a non-empty computational horizon:

  \mathrm{P} \neq \mathrm{NP} \Longleftrightarrow \exists L \text{ (NP-complete)} \text{ with } \mathcal{H}_c(L, q) \neq \varnothing.

The formal conjecture. For the QOU at a non-torsion substrate parameter q_0 \in \mathbb{G}_m^{\mathrm{nt}}(\mathbb{R}), there exists a family of braids \{L_N = \hat{\beta}_N\}_{N \geq 1} with c_N = 3N crossings encoding an NP-complete problem such that:

  \mathcal{H}_c(L_N, q_0) \neq \varnothing \qquad \text{for all } N \geq N_0.

This non-empty boundary establishes a genuine event horizon within the resolution tree, implying \mathrm{P} \neq \mathrm{NP} over \mathbb{R} at q = q_0.
